findings.location: Production activation and execution ownership, paragraph 2; plan.md AD-14 and Public-Seam Test-First Slice 10; research.md R-11 steps 1-7
findings.affected_requirement: Story 12.3 concurrent-analysis intent; FR-006; SC-001; Quality Review QR-001 correction outcome requiring shared-capacity continuation
findings.evidence: The corrected production path defines one single-flight pair pump that repeatedly claims one job, hydrates one packet, invokes exactly one Worker, commits or classifies that lease, and only then proceeds to the next claim. No normative plan or runtime-contract step launches and tracks multiple scoped job runners concurrently, fills available durable capacity, drains in-flight runners before reconciliation, or explains how a limit increase activates additional slots. The proposed production tests assert identity preservation and that the cap is not exceeded, but do not require observable overlap of two and four Worker executions. A strictly sequential implementation therefore conforms to the written AD-14 flow and can pass the named assertions while failing the story's bounded concurrent dispatch behavior and leaving the shared 1-4 capacity seam operationally unused.
findings.correction_outcome: Define one single-flight coordinator per pair with an explicit capacity-filling fan-out algorithm: repeatedly claim and launch independently scoped job runners until the durable store returns AtCapacity/ineligible work, observe runner completions without using completion order as claim or identity authority, stop launches immediately when the durable provider circuit or terminal failure closes dispatch, and reconcile only after the store proves terminal exhaustion and all in-flight runners are drained. Add production-composed tests that hold Workers at a controllable barrier and prove actual simultaneous execution reaches two and four when enough eligible jobs exist, never exceeds the effective durable limit, preserves existing leases across 4-to-1 changes, fills newly available capacity after 1-to-4 changes, and remains deterministic across completion schedules.

summary: REVISE. The corrected plan closes QR-002 through QR-005 with concrete, architecture-safe contracts: exactly five durable active source-free probes and no sixth or startup resume; lease/version/pair/circuit revalidation before navigation disclosure and receipt mutation; complete scalar reconstruction of the persisted canonical Document graph for replay; and executable authenticated PostgreSQL plus real Windows-host qualification. It also identifies the necessary DI owners and preserves the Story 12.1/12.2, immutable-Document, host-runtime, and Story 12.4/12.5 exclusion boundaries. QR-001 remains materially incomplete because AD-14 specifies a sequential claim-to-completion pump and no capacity-filling concurrent runner lifecycle. The plan is not yet ready for hash-bound planned-change authorization or task regeneration.
